status.glance: Layer 1 is complete, and Layer 2 is now close to it: `Spa(A,A⁺)` is spectral, rational subsets form a basis and are stable under intersection, perturbation and passage to a localisation, and the emptiness criterion holds without extra hypotheses. Layer 3 has coordinate rings, restriction maps and a candidate structure presheaf but no stalk theory; Layer 4 has the algebraic chain up to Proposition 8.30 and nothing past it; Layers 5 and 6 have not begun.

frontier.name: The completed coordinate ring `A_U = A⟨T/s⟩`
frontier.text: — carry the homeomorphism from the topological localisation `A(T/s)` to the completed one, prove `(A_U, A_U⁺)` is a Huber pair, and identify valuations and rational subsets across it. Everything in Layer 3 downstream waits on this.

frontier.name: Surjectivity of the rational evaluation map
frontier.text: — `A⟨X₁,…,Xₖ⟩ → A⟨T/s⟩` has dense range when the numerators and `s` generate the unit ideal; only closed range is missing. It would make `A⟨T/s⟩` strictly topologically of finite type, hence strongly noetherian over a strongly noetherian base, discharging the hypothesis Proposition 8.30 currently assumes.

frontier.name: Structure-presheaf local geometry
frontier.text: — identify the presentation limit with `A_U` on rational opens, define `𝒪_X⁺`, and prove that stalks are local with the point valuation supported at the maximal ideal. The residue-field valuations exist; nothing at stalk level does.

frontier.name: Tate acyclicity
frontier.text: — continue from Proposition 8.30 to Corollary 8.32, the two-piece Laurent cover of Lemma 8.33, and arbitrary finite rational covers. The last step needs Lemma 7.54, the standard rational refinement, which is not established.

frontier.name: Pre-adic spaces
frontier.text: — define `𝒱^pre`, its affinoid objects and the sheafiness predicates once the stalk package is in place; this is the entry point to Layers 5 and 6, both of which are empty.

frontier.name: Riemann–Roch
frontier.text: — what remains is the divisor `(ω)` of a nonzero Weil differential, the canonical class, and duality `L(W − D) ≅ Ω_F(D)`; with `dim_k Ω_F(D) = i(D)` in, duality is the whole theorem; uniqueness then yields `ℓ(W) = g` and `deg W = 2g − 2`.

frontier.text: — the `deg ≥ 2g − 1` regime, `ℓ(n·[0]) = n`, genus 0, Weierstrass gaps and `[Infinite k]` Clifford wait on Riemann–Roch; `η` and the completion comparison do not.

frontier.text: — finite support of `d(P′∣P)`, the tame value `d = e − 1` under residue separability, then the cotrace, which needs the canonical divisor of a Weil differential; Hurwitz is blocked on both.

frontier.name: Finite normalization (Layer 2)

frontier.text: — untouched; `Cl⁰(F) ≅ ClassGroup R` is not instantiated at `WeierstrassCurve`; nothing in the digest touches Mathlib's elliptic curves. Layer 12's contracts could be drafted now.

status.glance: Lane G has the whole chain-level package over `𝔽₂` — diagrams, moves, links, gradings, the bigrading, all three complexes, the grid determinant formula — but not `∂² = 0` in general, not invariance, and not the homology of any nontrivial diagram. Lane L has its first computed lattice homology and a `U`-tower in every negative-definite plumbing, in characteristic two and with no Neumann-move invariance. Lane ALG has the stabilization and filtered-colimit API the roadmap asked for; Lanes K and H have not begun.

frontier.text: The blocking case is where the two rectangles share exactly one side column: three of its four configurations still need the recut pairing each decomposition with a second one through a different intermediate state.

frontier.name: Grid homology of a nontrivial grid.
frontier.text: Every homology so far lives in size `n ≤ 2`, where the differential vanishes for lack of rectangles. The trefoil's `5 × 5` grid, the roadmap's first acceptance criterion, waits on `∂² = 0` and on rectangle counts that evaluate.

frontier.name: Commutation and stabilization invariance.
frontier.text: No pentagon-counting chain map or hexagon-counting homotopy exists; stabilization additionally wants the mapping-cone identification, which `GC⁻` now makes statable.

frontier.name: Lattice homology of `E₈`, and Neumann invariance.
frontier.text: Nonvanishing is known, the rank is not, and the literature's answer is over `ℤ[U]`. Invariance needs the blow-up results carried from the lattice up to the homology, plus the remaining Neumann moves.

frontier.name: Lane H (stable `HF̂`).
frontier.text: Untouched: pointed Heegaard diagram combinatorics, admissibility and the nice-move calculus are all still to be built, and no other lane feeds it.

status.glance: The Riemann mapping summit and layers L0–L5 are complete, including the Jordan-domain form of Carathéodory boundary correspondence. L6 is genuinely partial: the Schwarz–Christoffel integrand, primitive, boundary values, edges and prevertex asymptotics exist, but no theorem yet identifies a global map onto a prescribed polygon; prime ends remain outside the stated L5 milestone.

frontier.name: Schwarz–Christoffel polygon mapping.
frontier.text: Prove global injectivity and identify the image of the upper-half-plane primitive as the polygon bounded by the straight edge chain; the current declarations give only local conformality and intervalwise boundary injectivity.

frontier.name: The parameter problem.
frontier.text: For an arbitrary prescribed polygon, produce or characterize prevertices and exponents whose Schwarz–Christoffel boundary data realize its vertices and angles; no such existence result is established here.

frontier.name: Prime ends.
frontier.text: If boundary correspondence beyond Jordan domains is pursued, prime ends need their own definitions and theory; they are a follow-on target, not unfinished L5 work.

frontier.name: Mathlib reconciliation.
frontier.text: The roadmap calls for replacing duplicated L0–L3 proofs and deleting the local Riemann mapping theorem if Mathlib’s version lands, but the supplied material does not establish that this has happened.

Beyond Layer 0 only the contraction package of Layer 3 has been touched; no DG or `A∞` algebra has yet been defined.

The coderivation/Taylor correspondence, suspension, and both Stasheff sums are in place; this closes the arity 1–4 audit.

frontier.name: Remaining Layer 0 gaps for Layer 2

status.glance: The strict carrier (Layer 1), the counting and weak-regularity milestones of Layer 2, the AE view (Layer 3), the coupling/map agreement of Layer 5, and the forward half of separation (Layer 6a) are proved, with Goodman and Mantel as Layer 7 checks. What is genuinely partial is the cut metric itself: the arbitrary-carrier triangle inequality `cutDist_triangle` is not there, so `GraphonSpace` and every quotient-level statement wait on it. Compactness (Layer 4), the inverse counting converse, the convergence equivalence, and Layers 8–9 have not begun beyond the finite-graph density estimators.

frontier.name: `cutDist_triangle`
frontier.text: — the triangle inequality on arbitrary carriers (Janson, Lemma 6.5). Both validation milestones are in place: finite gluing with explicit null atoms, and step-approximation stability with its transfer lemma for an approximating intermediate graphon. What remains is the assembly: approximate by step graphons, glue the finite couplings, pass to the limit. Nothing quotient-level can start before this.

frontier.text: — the quotient by `cutDist = 0`, its `MetricSpace` instance, `GraphonSpaceI` and `homDensityOnSpace`; then density of step graphons in `δ□` (weak regularity already supplies the approximant) and total boundedness. Blocked only on the triangle inequality.

status.glance: The Mordell–Weil summit is proved, over Dedekind fraction fields and not only number fields, with the canonical height and regulator above it. The isogeny layer has an additive group of morphisms, kernels, the invariant differential with its separability criterion, and a formal group with points over a complete field, but not the quadratic degree form or the dual. The Weil pairing, the Hasse bound, the reduction filtration and Selmer/Sha have not begun.

frontier.name: The degree form on `Hom`.
frontier.text: What remains is the behaviour of `deg` under addition: the parallelogram law, bilinearity of `deg (φ + ψ) − deg φ − deg ψ`, and `n • 1 = [n]`. Additivity of composition in the inner variable would make `End` a ring.

frontier.name: `deg (1 − π) = #E(𝔽_q)` and the Hasse bound.
frontier.text: `1 − π` is separable with a finite kernel bounded by its degree; missing is equality of kernel size and degree for separable isogenies, then Cauchy–Schwarz on the degree form.

frontier.name: The dual isogeny.
frontier.text: The factorisation and fixed-field theorems are in place; still needed are base change to the separable closure, descent of the factor to the ground field, and the induced-place criterion that packages it as an isogeny.

frontier.name: `Ê(𝔪) ≅ E₁(K)` and the reduction filtration.
frontier.text: The formal group's points map onto the points with a pole in `x`; identifying those with the kernel of reduction needs a reduction map on points over a DVR, which does not exist yet.

frontier.name: The Weil pairing.
frontier.text: Divisor evaluation is built; still needed are a function with divisor `N(P) − N(O)`, Weil reciprocity, and the dual.

frontier.text: Prove that the successor array of a recurrent Markov-exchangeable process is row exchangeable; the existing [row-exchangeable successor-array bridge](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/Exchangeability/DiaconisFreedman.html#TauCeti.Probability.mixedMarkovChain_of_rowExchangeable_successorProcess) then yields a mixture of Markov chains. The landed last-exit admissibility machinery supplies the finite row permutations needed for this step.

frontier.text: Starting from an arbitrary jointly or separately exchangeable array, construct a measurable coding by the canonical global, vertex and cell noises. The current theory proves row-wise conditional i.i.d.-ness, coupled row coding, dissociation, and that every such coding is exchangeable, but only this forward direction.

frontier.name: Gluing along the boundary
frontier.text: — the spine. Boundary manifold and local collars exist; a global collar `∂M × [0,1)` is the missing step before `glue`, with Dehn filling and connected sum blocked behind it.

frontier.name: The `C^∞` topology on `Diff(M)`
frontier.text: — the group and `O(n+1) → Diff(Sⁿ)` exist; the initial topology in charts for compact `M` makes that inclusion continuous and the Smale conjecture stateable.

frontier.name: Knot diagrams, or a Seifert matrix of a knot
frontier.text: — the Alexander polynomial has no knot behind it. A diagram type with Reidemeister moves is the hub of the README's spanning tree and what Markov's theorem needs; either route makes the polynomial an invariant.

frontier.name: Zeeman's conjecture as a statement
frontier.text: — collapsibility and the ordered cylinder `K × I` exist; only a contractible-2-complex predicate remains. The nearest Kirby-list target.

frontier.name: Combinatorial manifold implies PL manifold
frontier.text: — both sides exist, but the realization has only the weak topology and no charts; a PL atlas on the polyhedron comes first.

rows.name: GlobalNumberFields
rows.title: global number fields, ray classes, adeles, and Hecke characters
layers: Layer 0: places, completions, and the product formula

Layer 2: moduli and ray class carriers

Layer 8: finite extensions of adeles and ideles
Layer 9: Hecke and ray class characters
Layer 10: archimedean characters, infinity types, and cyclotomic arithmetic
Layer 11: orders and Picard groups

status.glance: The roadmap has just begun. Its Layer 1 headline theorem, mixed-place weak approximation, is done, and Layer 0 has a normalized absolute value on each infinite completion. Everything else, from the finite side of Layer 0 through moduli, ray class groups, ideal counting, adeles, ideles, Hecke characters, infinity types, cyclotomic arithmetic, and orders, has not been started.

frontier.name: Finish Layer 0
frontier.text: — define the finite-place normalized absolute value on `v.adicCompletion K`, prove the uniformizer convention and agreement with the valuation, then prove finiteness of the support of `|x|_v ≠ 1` and transport the product formula. The finite side depends on the finite-completion dictionary consumed from Number Field Arithmetic; whether that dictionary is available is not established here.

frontier.name: Finish Layer 1
frontier.text: — derive the `Kˣ` corollaries of weak approximation and build the total sign homomorphism with its surjectivity on `Kˣ`, which is what Layer 2's narrow-class obstruction is phrased against. No blocker beyond the theorem already in place.

frontier.name: Layer 2, moduli and ray class carriers
frontier.text: — `Modulus`, `congruenceSubgroup`, `idealsPrimeTo`, `RayClassGroup`, and `idealClass` with the intrinsic triviality criterion. This is the next thing every downstream consumer needs, and it requires `idealsAway` and `integralIdealsAway` from Number Field Arithmetic.

frontier.name: Layers 4 and 5, the adelic spine
frontier.text: — the placewise API of Mathlib's finite adeles, discreteness of `K` and compactness of `𝔸_K/K`. These can proceed in parallel with Layer 2 and need only Mathlib and Layer 0.

frontier.name: Layer 3, uniform ray-class ideal counting
frontier.text: — the power-saving lattice-point count and its assembly into `rayClassIdealCount`, which Chebotarev consumes. It waits on Layer 2 and is the largest single piece of work in the roadmap.

rows.title: Grothendieck groups, Cartan maps, and Euler forms

Layer 5: finite-support Euler characteristics and Ext-Euler descent
Layer 6: Laurent coefficients, q-Euler forms, and specialization
Layer 7: left and right numerical Grothendieck groups

status.glance: The categorical spine is in place: exact structures, the presentation engine, the four Grothendieck groups with graded ℤ-actions and Laurent module structure, the projective resolution theorem, Euler–Poincaré, the Ext-Euler pairing and numerical quotients. Genuinely partial are the graded Euler form (defined, but neither sesquilinear nor descended to the Laurent K₀), the bounded-complex comparisons and general resolving subcategories; Layer 4 and every worked example have not begun.

frontier.name: Sesquilinear q-Euler form
frontier.text: — descend `gradedExtEuler` to `LaurentK0` instead of exact K₀ and prove `χ_q(M{1},N) = q⁻¹χ_q(M,N)` and `χ_q(M,N{1}) = qχ_q(M,N)` using `LaurentPolynomial.invert`; the reindexing lemma ([`TauCeti.targetShiftGradedDimension_reindex_add`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/EulerCharacteristic/GradedDimension.html#TauCeti.targetShiftGradedDimension_reindex_add)) gives the shift identity at graded-dimension level.

frontier.name: Dual-numbers rejection and the other worked examples
frontier.text: — the README makes this test a precondition for accepting Ext-Euler descent, and descent has landed without it; the vector-space check needs nothing further, while `1 ⟶ 2` and E₈ wait on Layer 4.

frontier.name: Layer 4, the Cartan map
frontier.text: — nothing exists; needs the quiver roadmap's projective covers and simples, then `K₀(proj A) ⟶ G₀(mod A)` from the induced split structure, the resolution theorem supplying the finite-global-dimension isomorphism.

frontier.name: Specialisation at `q = ±1` and comparison after forgetting the grading
frontier.text: — `laurentEval` and the forgetful K₀ map ([`TauCeti.GradedExactStructure.map_shiftEquiv_of_commShift`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/GrothendieckGroup/Graded.html#TauCeti.GradedExactStructure.map_shiftEquiv_of_commShift)) exist; base change of `LaurentK0`, the factoring theorem and the graded/ungraded Ext comparison hypotheses do not.

frontier.name: Bounded-complex comparisons and general resolving subcategories
frontier.text: — split K₀ to the triangulated K₀ of the bounded homotopy category, the derived comparison, and Weibel's Theorem II.7.6 with kernel closure, beyond the projective case.

rows.name: HeegaardFloer
rows.title: Heegaard Floer homology, analytically
layers: Lane M: Morse homology
Lane F0: the nonlinear-analysis substrate
Lane F1: the Cauchy–Riemann elliptic package
Lane F2: J-holomorphic curves
Lane F3: Lagrangian Floer homology, exact case
Lane F4: Heegaard Floer homology, holomorphically
Lane F5: beyond

status.glance: The Morse–Sard and Sard–Smale summits are complete, and much of Lane F0's abstract nonlinear Fredholm substrate is now available. Lane M, the manifold-level definitions in F2.1, and the symmetric-power geometry in F4.1 are genuinely partial; the Cauchy–Riemann package, every Floer homology theory, holomorphic `HF̂`, Lane F5, and the reconciliations have not begun in the recorded declarations.

frontier.name: Stable-manifold theorem
frontier.text: — turn the Morse normal form and gradient-flow foundations into local stable and unstable submanifolds; this is the nearest missing step in Lane M and precedes the λ-lemma.

frontier.name: Morse–Smale moduli spaces
frontier.text: — use finite-dimensional Sard to obtain transverse stable/unstable intersections, then prove broken-trajectory compactness and gluing before defining the differential and showing its square is zero.

frontier.name: Fredholm sections and strip operators
frontier.text: — lift the map-level regular-value theory to sections of Banach bundles and prove `d/ds + A(s)` Fredholm with the intended index; the latter depends on the Sobolev and elliptic work of Lane F1.

frontier.name: The Cauchy–Riemann elliptic package
frontier.text: — build the required `W^{k,p}` spaces on strips and surfaces, trace and multiplication results, Calderón–Zygmund estimates, totally real boundary regularity, and Riemann–Roch with boundary. This remains the long pole for every holomorphic moduli space.

frontier.name: Smooth symmetric powers
frontier.text: — prove smooth or complex compatibility of the elementary-symmetric charts, then construct the `Sym^g(Σ)` geometry, the totally real tori, and the basepoint divisor required by F4.1.

rows.name: HodgeStructures
rows.title: Hodge structures (pure, mixed, and polarized)
layers: L0 — Pure Hodge structures; the Hodge decomposition
L1 — Polarization & Hodge–Riemann; semisimplicity (summit of the pure theory)
L2 — Mixed Hodge structures; strictness (Deligne)
L3 — Period-domain points; the symmetry group

status.glance: All four milestones — the L0 Hodge decomposition, L1 semisimplicity, L2 strictness and the L3 Hodge-number partition — are proved, and the core definitions have the shape the README specifies. Partial: the L2 companions (coarse conjugation relation on Deligne's bigrading; no abelian structure on the mixed category) and the worked instances (Tate complete, the effective weight-one instance not built). No layer is untouched.

frontier.name: The fine conjugation relation on Deligne's bigrading
frontier.text: — prove conj I^{p,q} ≡ I^{q,p} modulo ⨆_{r<p,s<q} I^{r,s}; the landed statement is modulo the whole weight step W_{p+q−2}, and the bigrading API it needs (independence, recovery of W) is in place.

frontier.name: The abelian category of mixed Hodge structures
frontier.text: — kernels and cokernels of morphisms as mixed Hodge structures, from strictness; the preadditive ℚ-linear category and both strictness theorems exist.

frontier.name: The effective weight-one instance
frontier.text: — a polarized effective weight-1 structure from (Λ ≅ ℤ^{2g}, J, E), the abelian-variety case; the real form so far enters only as the fixed points of the conjugation inside `realAlmostComplexStructure`, and a first-class V_ℝ with its structure map is the prerequisite.

frontier.name: Internal Hom of pure Hodge structures
frontier.text: — the last L0 companion; dual and tensor product exist, so Hom(V,W) = V^∨ ⊗ W is within reach.

frontier.name: The composed base-change witness
frontier.text: — `IsBaseChange ℂ (ι_{ℚℂ} ∘ₗ ι_ℚ)` from the two legs, so the tower is consumed as a property instead of transported along `rationalToComplexLinearEquiv`.

rows.name: HopfRinow
rows.title: geodesics, the exponential map, and the Hopf–Rinow theorem
layers: Layer 0: the reconciled Riemannian distance
Layer 1: the geodesic equation, the flow, and the exponential map
Layer 2: normal neighbourhoods, the Gauss lemma, and minimizing geodesics
Layer 3: the Hopf–Rinow equivalence
Layer 4: corollaries and downstream theory

status.glance: Layer 0, the reconciled Riemannian distance, is done up to two loose ends, and the connection half of Layer 1 is done: the Levi-Civita connection exists, is unique and `C^∞`, the along-curve derivative and the geodesic predicate are in place, and geodesics have constant speed. The geodesic spray, its flow, and the exponential map are not built, so Layers 2 and 3 have not begun; Layer 4's length-space and geodesic-space API exists, but its Riemannian instance waits on Layer 3.

frontier.name: The geodesic spray
frontier.text: — define `S` on `TM`, prove its chart formula `(x, v) ↦ (v, -Γ_x(v, v))` chart-independent using the Christoffel transformation law now in place, deduce `C^∞` from the smooth Christoffel map, and identify its integral curves with velocity lifts of geodesics. Everything below waits on this.

frontier.name: Local existence, maximal intervals, and homogeneity
frontier.text: — apply the maximal integral curve and the extension criterion to `S` to get `J(p,v)`; the affine reparametrization lemma is ready for `γ_{p,λv}(t) = γ_{p,v}(λt)`.

frontier.name: Smooth dependence and the local geodesic flow
frontier.text: — no `C^k`-dependence theorem for ODE solutions has landed, so this is new analysis rather than assembly.

frontier.name: The exponential map and its derivative at zero
frontier.text: — `expDomain p`, openness, smoothness, and the identity derivative; the manifold inverse function theorem then gives a local diffeomorphism at `0`.

frontier.name: Layer 0 loose ends and the Riemannian geodesic-space instance
frontier.text: — regular reparametrization and `pathELength`-form lower semicontinuity are self-contained; the geodesic-space instance for a complete connected manifold is blocked on `(f_p)`.

rows.name: JacobianChallenge
rows.title: the Jacobian challenge (Christian Merten's AG version)
layers: Layer A, line bundles, divisors, Picard group, degree
Layer B, coherent cohomology over `k`: genus, Riemann–Roch, Serre duality
Layer C, relative coherent cohomology and base change
Layer D, the relative Picard functor and the Jacobian scheme
Layer E, abelian varieties
Layer F, Abel–Jacobi and the universal property

status.glance: No layer is complete, and neither the Picard scheme nor the Jacobian has been constructed. Layer A is the strongest part of the roadmap; Layers B and E now have substantial foundations but remain partial, while Layers C, D and F have not begun.

frontier.name: The Picard group and divisor–line-bundle dictionary.
frontier.text: Pass from tensorable line bundles to their group of isomorphism classes, construct inverses, and prove the correspondence with divisors modulo principal divisors.

frontier.name: Finiteness and vanishing for coherent cohomology.
frontier.text: Prove affine acyclicity, finite-dimensionality for proper coherent sheaves, and `H²=0` for curves; the present Euler-characteristic theorem assumes the needed finiteness and vanishing.

frontier.name: Riemann–Roch and Serre duality.
frontier.text: Construct the relative dualizing sheaf and prove duality, Riemann–Roch, and agreement between divisor degree and `χ(L)-χ(𝒪_X)` after the cohomological prerequisites.

frontier.name: Relative cohomology and symmetric powers.
frontier.text: Build proper-flat pushforward, cohomology and base change, semicontinuity, relative effective Cartier divisors, and `Symᵈ X`, which the Abel-map route to representability needs.

frontier.name: The Picard scheme and Abel–Jacobi map.
frontier.text: Define and rigidify the fppf Picard functor, prove representability and properness of `Pic⁰`, then construct the Jacobian and establish its universal property and base-change compatibility.

Layer 2: Hecke operators and the Hecke algebra

status.glance: The general-level valence formula of Layer 1 is complete. The Hecke, Petersson, newform, and Atkin–Lehner layers now have substantial working infrastructure—including the classical prime action, bundled newforms, squarefree descent, and normalized Fricke involutions—but their main adjoint, decomposition, multiplicity-one, and sign theorems remain partial; the coefficient-field, LMFDB, trace-formula, and modular-curve dimension-formula summits have not begun.

frontier.name: The Atkin–Lehner Main Lemma.
frontier.text: Assemble the coprime filters, prime-by-prime descent, factor dichotomy, and squarefree decomposition into the global statement that vanishing at every index coprime to `N` forces oldness.

frontier.name: Petersson adjoints.
frontier.text: Prove `T_n* = ⟨n⟩⁻¹T_n` at good indices, then obtain normality and simultaneous diagonalization on each character space.

frontier.name: The full classical Hecke action.
frontier.text: Extend the prime-generator comparison to composite and prime-power Hecke-ring elements, keeping the scalar normalization explicit.

frontier.name: Bad-prime newform theory.
frontier.text: Establish newspace stability under `U_p`, upgrade newforms to full eigenforms, and prove the bad-prime eigenvalue classification.

frontier.name: Multiplicity one and conductor uniqueness.
frontier.text: Prove equality of newforms, not merely equality of their good eigenvalues, first in a fixed character space and then across levels; the latter is needed for uniqueness of the primitive pair.

rows.name: Multiquadratic
rows.title: multiquadratic fields and genus theory
layers: Layer 0: the multiquadratic field
Layer 1: the prime-splitting law
Layer 2: the 2-elementary quotient of the class group
Layer 3: the genus field and the 2-rank theorem

status.glance: The multiquadratic, splitting, and field-theoretic genus-field layers are established, and the imaginary quadratic 2-rank summit is complete. The class-group comparison is still partial—the real narrow formula and an actual `Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl(K)/Cl(K)²` are absent—and the long-horizon class-field constructions have not begun.

frontier.name: Real narrow 2-rank formula
frontier.text: — descend the coprime-ideal genus characters to enough independent characters of `Cl⁺(K)/Cl⁺(K)²` to complement the existing upper bound and prove `rank₂ Cl⁺(K) = t - 1`.

frontier.name: Galois group versus `Cl/Cl²`
frontier.text: — construct the actual reciprocity or Artin map giving `Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl(K)/Cl(K)²`; for imaginary quadratic fields only equality of the two finite cardinalities is established.

frontier.name: Ambiguous class number formula
frontier.text: — upgrade the ambiguous-ideal descent and resulting rank bounds to the formula requested in Layer 2.

frontier.name: Remaining worked examples
frontier.text: — state and discharge `[ℚ(√2,√3):ℚ] = 4` and the degree `2^(g+1)` of the Erdős CM family; neither conclusion appears among the supplied declarations.

rows.name: NumberFieldArithmetic
rows.title: number fields, ramification, Frobenius, and the LMFDB invariants
layers: Layer 1: the splitting dictionary
Layer 2: Frobenius elements and the Artin symbol
Layer 3: the index, Dedekind–Kummer, and Dedekind's theorem
Layer 4: the relative discriminant
Layer 5: the global-local dictionary at finite places
Layer 6: global ramification consequences
Layer 7: subfields, integral bases, monogenicity, and explicit units
Layer 8: the intrinsic label prefix and the invariant suite

status.glance: Layers 2.1 and 2.2 are done, Layer 2.3 has its definition and one characterising lemma but none of its comparison API, and Layer 1.1's count criterion is published. Nothing else has begun: Layers 1.2 to 1.5, 2.4 to 2.7, and all of Layers 3 to 8 have no declarations.

frontier.name: Layer 2.4, functoriality of the Frobenius
frontier.text: — restriction along `AlgEquiv.restrictNormal`, then `artinSymbol_map_restrictNormalHom` and the tower formula `exists_isArithFrobAt_pow_inertiaDeg`. Its prerequisites, Layers 2.1 and 2.3, now exist, and both names are the Chebotarev contract.

frontier.name: The rest of Layer 2.3's API
frontier.text: — conjugation covariance `Frob (σ • Q) = σ (Frob Q) σ⁻¹`, `orderOf (Frob Q) = f`, `zpowers = stabilizer` at an unramified `Q`, the image under `stabilizerHom` being the residue Frobenius, and the corollary at `span {p}` over `ℚ`.

frontier.name: Layer 2.5, the ideal-theoretic Artin map
frontier.text: — `idealsAway`, `artinHomAway`, and the five named lemmas; blocked on Layer 2.4.

frontier.name: Layers 1.3 and 1.4
frontier.text: — the decomposition and inertia dictionary and the double-coset law `doubleCosetEquiv`, which Dedekind's theorem in Layer 3.9 needs.

frontier.name: Layers 3.1 to 3.5 and 4.1
frontier.text: — the power-basis index, the index formula, and the `relDiscr` definition; independent of Layer 2 and available now.

rows.name: OneParameterSemigroups
rows.title: one-parameter semigroups, completely monotone and positive-definite functions, and Bochner-type representations
layers: Part A — Strongly continuous semigroups
Part B — Completely monotone (and Bernstein) functions
Part C — Positive-definite functions and Bochner's theorem

status.glance: Every named non-stretch milestone is now established: Hille–Yosida and Lumer–Phillips generation, the abstract Cauchy problem, Bernstein’s theorem, Bochner’s theorem, and the Berg–Christensen–Ressel representation. Complex resolvent analyticity and the Stieltjes correspondences remain partial; the C₀-group/Stone stretch has substantial foundations but not the full unbounded theorem, while the LCA/Pontryagin extension has not begun.

frontier.name: Complex resolvent analyticity
frontier.text: — construct the complexified generator and prove holomorphy on its complex resolvent set; the current declarations provide the real-parameter resolvent identity and derivative formulas, not this bridge.

frontier.name: Stieltjes correspondences
frontier.text: — complete the converse characterizations around completely monotone and Bernstein functions; what is established here is that Stieltjes functions are completely monotone and that multiplication by the parameter admits a Bernstein extension.

frontier.name: Stone’s theorem
frontier.text: — extend the unitary-group theory from skew-adjointness of an existing generator and the bounded self-adjoint exponential example to the general unbounded self-adjoint generation theorem.

frontier.name: LCA Bochner theory
frontier.text: — no Pontryagin-duality generalization is established here; as the roadmap notes, this stretch depends on suitable upstream LCA support.

rows.name: OptimalTransport
rows.title: optimal transport and Wasserstein geometry
layers: Layer 0: transport plans, maps, kernels, and gluing
Layer 1: transport cost, compactness, existence, and stability
Layer 2: Kantorovich duality, transforms, and optimality certificates
Layer 3: Wasserstein distances and topology
Layer 4: the Monge problem and abstract transport maps
Layer 5: convex analysis, Brenier, and polar factorization
Layer 6: Monge--Ampère measures, equations, and regularity
Layer 7: Riemannian Brenier--McCann transport
Layer 8: metric curves, dynamic plans, and Benamou--Brenier
Layer 9: displacement geometry and convexity
Layer 10: abstract metric gradient flows
Layer 11: entropy, Wasserstein differential calculus, JKO, and PDE flows
Layer 12: Fréchet and Wasserstein barycenters
Layer 13: entropic transport, Sinkhorn, and Schrödinger bridges
Layer 14: synthetic curvature, nonsmooth heat flow, and optimal maps
Layer 15: measured kernels and Gromov--Wasserstein
Layer 16: public API, extraction, and end-to-end examples

status.glance: Layer 0 (plans, maps, kernels, gluing) and Layer 1 (transport cost, compactness, existence, stability) are done, and Layer 2 has weak duality, the `c`-transform calculus, finite and compact strong duality, and optimality certificates. Layer 2's Polish duality, dual attainment, and Borel-cost regimes have not begun, nor has anything from Layer 3 (Wasserstein distances) onward.

frontier.name: Polish lower-semicontinuous Kantorovich duality
frontier.text: (Layer 2, item 4) — the theorem for `c ≥ a ⊕ b` with `a, b` upper semicontinuous and integrable, comparing bounded-continuous and integrable dual classes, then dual attainment under an integrable split upper envelope. The compact theorem and the bounded-below interface are in place; the passage to the Polish space remains. This is Layer 2's named summit.

frontier.name: The `W_p` distance
frontier.text: (Layer 3, item 1) — define it over couplings through `eLpNorm` of `edist` for `p : ℝ≥0∞`, and prove the triangle inequality by gluing plus Minkowski. Gluing and existence for `edist ^ p` are ready; every later layer waits on this.

frontier.name: Schachermayer–Teichmann on Polish spaces
frontier.text: (Layer 2, item 7) — the converse: a finite-cost plan concentrated on a `c`-cyclically monotone set is optimal, for finite-valued lower-semicontinuous costs. The forward direction and the finite case are done; the converse needs a contact-potential construction not yet started.

frontier.name: Small Layer 1 and 2 gaps
frontier.text: — finite multi-marginal dual attainment, the lower-semicontinuity lemma for costs bounded below by integrable marginal terms, and the Layer 0 and Layer 1 acceptance checks. All self-contained.

frontier.name: Borel-cost regimes
frontier.text: (Layer 2, item 5) — Beiglböck–Schachermayer for finite nonnegative Borel costs and the relaxed primal of Beiglböck–Léonard–Schachermayer. Untouched; depends on the Polish duality theorem above.

rows.name: PDE
rows.title: partial differential equations
layers: Lane A: function spaces on a domain
Lane B: harmonic-analysis estimates
Lane C: maximum principles and potential theory
Lane D: linear elliptic existence
Lane E: elliptic regularity
Lane F: parabolic and evolution equations

status.glance: Lane D, linear elliptic existence by the energy method, is complete through the spectrum: the Dirichlet problem has a unique weak solution, the Fredholm alternative holds, and the Dirichlet eigenfunctions form an orthonormal basis of `L²(Ω)`. Lane A is done for the zero-boundary spaces `W^{k,p}_0(Ω)` and thin for `W^{k,p}(Ω)`, which has no density theorem, trace or extension. Lane C is still partly planar and has no Green's function; Lane B stops at the maximal function; Lanes E and F are untouched.

frontier.name: Meyers-Serrin and the density gap.
frontier.text: Convolution with a smooth compactly supported kernel is known to commute with the weak derivative; what remains is `C^∞ ∩ W^{k,p}` density, which needs no boundary regularity and would let `W^{k,p}(Ω)` statements be checked on smooth functions alone.

frontier.name: Trace and extension on `W^{1,p}(Ω)`.
frontier.text: Only zero-extension out of `W^{1,p}_0(Ω)` exists. A trace with kernel `W^{1,p}_0` and an extension into `W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ)` for Lipschitz `∂Ω` would carry Rellich, and the spectral package with it, to the full space.

frontier.name: The mean-value property on `ℝⁿ`.
frontier.text: Harnack and the strong maximum principle are still planar, resting on Mathlib's complex harmonic theory; the `n`-dimensional mean-value characterisation is the single result that would lift both.

frontier.name: `-ΔG = δ`.
frontier.text: The kernel and its sphere flux are done; the distributional identity, then Green's function, Poisson kernel and Perron's method, are the rest of Lane C.

frontier.name: Interior `H²` regularity.
frontier.text: The first step of Lane E, by difference quotients, and what would upgrade the weak solutions now in hand. Schauder and De Giorgi-Nash-Moser beyond it wait on Lane B.

rows.name: PolynomialGaloisGroups
rows.title: Galois groups of polynomials
layers: Layer 0: the permutation representation of a polynomial
Layer 1: permutation groups, blocks, and wreath products
Layer 2: the dictionary between Galois theory and permutations
Layer 3: the discriminant and the alternating group
Layer 4: resolvents
Layer 5: Frobenius specialization
Layer 6: transitive subgroups of `Sₙ` for `n ≤ 5`, and the label predicates
Layer 9: `Sₙ` as a Galois group over `ℚ`

status.glance: Four pull requests have landed, all in the roadmap's opening layers: Layer 0's degree bookkeeping, most of the API for cycle types that count fixed points, and two of Layer 1's recognition theorems. Everything else, from the orbit dictionary and wreath products through discriminants, resolvents, Frobenius specialization, the labels in degree at most five, and the realization of Sₙ over ℚ, has not begun.

frontier.name: The remaining recognition theorems of Layer 1
frontier.text: — the transposition-in-prime-degree statement, the odd-power-is-a-transposition lemma, and the primitive-with-transposition and primitive-with-3-cycle statements. The README records that Mathlib supplies the last two and the main ingredient of the first; with the two landed theorems they complete the four group-theoretic steps of Layer 9.

frontier.name: `fullCycleType` as the roadmap spells it
frontier.text: — the name is the contract with Number Field Arithmetic and an export to Belyi Maps, and the contract check in `Suggested.lean` needs the exact shape `cycleType + replicate (card − support.card) 1` at the carrier's own `DecidableEq` instance. status.glance: Layers 0 to 4 are done: every scalar family the roadmap names exists as a measure with its density or mass formula, closed-form cdf, moments, transforms and parameter measurability, and the classical relations among the families are proved. Layer 5 is partial, and Layer 6 has its symmetric-matrix carrier but no Wishart theory.

frontier.name: The multivariate Gaussian density
frontier.text: — the density against volume on `EuclideanSpace ℝ ι` for positive-definite covariance, singularity otherwise, and the Bochner mean. The affine change of variables from the isotropic product density is the intended route.

frontier.name: The multinomial mean and covariance
frontier.text: — the Euclidean mean, the entrywise covariance as `covMatrix` with its `covarianceBilin` corollary, the characteristic function, and aggregation along a map of index types. The law, its masses and its directional mgf are in place.

frontier.name: Cholesky and the multivariate Gamma integral
frontier.text: — the equivalence between positive-definite symmetric matrices and positive-diagonal lower-triangular ones, its Jacobian in those coordinates, and the resulting integral over the positive-definite cone. Both gate the Wishart density; the carrier they need now exists.

frontier.name: The Wishart families
frontier.text: — the nonsingular real-degree density family and the natural-degree Gaussian-Gram family, their trace transforms and spectral characteristic function, and their agreement for positive-definite scale and degree at least the dimension. The quadratic-form mgf supplies the transforms; the density needs the two items above.

frontier.name: Dirichlet
frontier.text: — the whole family: the normalization chart, the lower-dimensional density, the Beta coordinate marginal, mean and covariance. Its Gamma-Beta prerequisite is now proved.

status.glance: Every stage of the roadmap now has its stated targets proved: the universal cover is constructed, the correspondence between subgroups of `π₁(X, x₀)` and connected covers is a bijection in both the pointed and unpointed forms, covers are classified categorically by fundamental-groupoid actions, and the application list (`π₁(S¹)`, `π_n(S¹)`, tori, `K(G, 1)`, `RPⁿ`) is complete. What remains lies outside the roadmap's own text: higher homotopy groups beyond vanishing statements, and the standing local hypotheses on the base, which no result here dispenses with.

frontier.name: Higher homotopy of `RPⁿ` and of spheres.
frontier.text: The covering isomorphism gives `π_k(RPⁿ) ≅ π_k(Sⁿ)` for `k ≥ 2`, but nothing here computes `π_n(Sⁿ)`, so no concrete group results. That needs a degree or Hurewicz argument, and neither appears here.

frontier.name: The fibre functor and its automorphisms.
frontier.text: The finite covers are proved to be a Galois category with the fibre over `x₀` as fibre functor, but the automorphism group of that functor is not identified. Mathlib's `IsFundamentalGroup`/`toAutMulEquiv` interface is the natural target; for infinite `π₁` that automorphism group is not `π₁` itself.

frontier.name: Existence of `K(G, 1)` spaces for an arbitrary group.
frontier.text: What is proved is recognition: a space with weakly contractible universal cover is a `K(G, 1)`, and covers of aspherical spaces are aspherical, with circles and tori as examples. No construction realising a given group as a fundamental group is present.

frontier.name: The standing local hypotheses.
frontier.text: Path-connectedness of the base has been removed from the groupoid-level classification, but local path-connectedness and semilocal simple connectivity are assumed throughout, and nothing here addresses bases failing them.

status.glance: Both named summits are reached: the Hermite functions are a complete orthonormal basis of `L²(ℝ)` and the Chebyshev polynomials a complete orthonormal basis of their weighted `L²`, assembled from one family-agnostic layer that also produces the weighted-measure and multidimensional bases. What remains is not a missing theorem but missing packaging: expansion API for the non-Hermite bases, and operator-level statements.

frontier.name: Expansion API for the Chebyshev and Gaussian Hermite bases
frontier.text: — Parseval exists generically and concretely for the Hermite functions, but the coefficient, summability and expansion lemmas have no counterpart yet for `chebyshevTHilbertBasis` or `gaussianHermiteHilbertBasis`. Pure specialization; no blocker.

frontier.name: The Fourier transform as a diagonalized operator on `L²(ℝ)`
frontier.text: — lifting the `(-i)ⁿ` eigenrelation from the pointwise integral to a unitary on `Lp` needs the rescaled `Φₙ` packaged as `L²` vectors and identified with a dilation of `hermiteFunctionLp`.

frontier.name: Ladder operators on `L²`
frontier.text: — `a` and `a†` as continuous linear operators with `[a,a†] = 1`. The identities are already available at Schwartz level via [`hermiteSchwartzMap`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Hermite/Function/Schwartz.html#TauCeti.hermiteSchwartzMap), which is exactly the form the roadmap wanted so the operator packaging costs no reproving.

frontier.text: — out of scope as stated, and the roadmap's reason still holds: those families would have to be defined before any `L²` basis statement about them can be made.
